newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Weather mostly good in Brazil soybean areas - coops.
newsitem.headline: Weather mostly good in Brazil soybean areas - coops.

text.p: Conditions were mostly favourable in Brazil's key soybean growing regions as the weather cleared in Parana, temporarily alleviating the problem of excess rains that has affected the state.
"We had excessive rains until yesterday," said Nivaldo Sandri, agronomist at the Copacol cooperative in Cafelandia. "But the weather has cleared up today."
It was too early to evaluate the damage to quality and productivity for soybeans, although for corn there would be a 20 to 30 percent crop loss, he added.
In Prudentopolis, the heavy rains damaged mainly the so-called precocious cycle soybean crop, said Ademar Dressler, agronomist at the Camp cooperative.
"It really damaged the crop quite a lot, especially the precocious variety," he said.
But skies were clear and the weather appeared to be normalising, Dressler said, adding that the early harvest was due to start today.
In Rio Grande do Sul, light rains continued to restore moisture to areas parched during a mostly dry December and January.
"We have good heat and humidity and the soybean is now developing well, it is recovering," said Flavio Nai, agronomist at the Coorondinha cooperative in Rondinha.

He estimated productivity would be down 10 to 15 percent this year because of the earlier dry weather but said further expected rains should limit the losses. --Joelle Diderich, Sao Paulo newsroom +55 11 248 5417
